verdict.rationale: Temporal documents a first-party self-hosted deployment path (Docker, Kubernetes, or manual), which lets the operator control where the Temporal Service and its workflow data physically reside. Archival to blob storage and multi-cluster replication add some control over where data goes. However, nothing in the evidence shows explicit region selection or data-residency guarantees for Temporal Cloud. Residency control is only implied through running your own infrastructure. missing for 10: Temporal Cloud region selection for Namespaces, documented data-residency/compliance guarantees, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Choose a deployment approach (Docker, Kubernetes, or manual) and set up a production-ready Temporal Service.
Archival: Move closed Workflow Histories and Visibility records to blob storage for longer retention.
Multi-Cluster Replication: Replicate Workflow state across clusters for failover and disaster recovery.
